A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Victorian system was established through an iterative, adaptive process that involved the participation of a broad range of stakeholder groups and the development of a comprehensive network of MPAs.
it was not a single factor that led to the development of the Victorian MPA network but a combination of factors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a comprehensive, adequate, and representative MPA network is possible in relatively small and relatively developed countries.

the development of a comprehensive and adequate system of highly protected MPAs is possible, but requires the following: (1) a long-term commitment from government to develop a comprehensive and adequate network of MPAs; (2) a commitment from all stakeholders to the development of an adequate network of MPA; (3) a willingness by government to engage with stakeholders and to listen and learn from them; (4) a willingness by stakeholders to compromise on their preferred outcomes to enable the development of an MPA
